items.title: A 13-storey residential building with 144 apartments is being considered for Bough Beeches Boulevard in Mississauga
items.summary: A proposed 144-unit development on Bough Beeches Boulevard would add new rental housing while retaining an existing 20-storey tower on the site. A 13-storey rental apartment building with 144 units is being proposed at 1315 Bough Beeches Blvd. in Mississauga. The City of Mississauga is reviewing an application to amend the official plan and zoning bylaw to permit a 13-storey rental apartment building at 1315 Bough Beeches Blvd. near Dixie and Rathburn roads in the Rathwood neighbourhood. The building would feature 144 residential units. 37-hectare site contains a 20-storey “tower-in-the-park” rental apartment building surrounded by two surface parking lots, according to the applicant’s planning rationale report. The existing building has 270 units. The property also contains a “vast area of open space with mature trees, a tennis court and a basketball court and a ramp to the underground parking garage, all of which will be retained … save for some surface parking,” said the planning rationale report, which was prepared by WND Associates Ltd. The existing building would also be retained. One- and two-storey homes that front Poltava Crescent are located north of the site while Rathburn Road and Rockwood Mall, which is a dated single-storey strip plaza, is to the south, according to the applicant’s report. Bough Beeches Boulevard, a mid-rise apartment building and homes are to the east; Dixie Road and a subdivision with townhouses and detached homes are to the west. The 13-storey building would feature residential units on levels 2 to 13 while the ground floor would house the lobby, amenity areas and loading/servicing spaces, according to the planning rationale report.

items.title: Man, child from the U.S. seriously injured in multi-vehicle collision on Mississauga highway
items.summary: Westbound lanes of Highway 403 at Mavis Road were closed for over five hours Tuesday evening for the investigation. m. on Tuesday, conducting an investigation and cleaning up the highway. A man and a child from the United States were seriously injured after they were struck by a vehicle while standing on the side of Hwy. 403 in Mississauga following a previous crash. m. on Tuesday in the westbound lanes of Highway 403, beyond Mavis Road. Two vehicles had collided, and the drivers moved their vehicles to the right shoulder of the highway before the occupants left their vehicles to exchange contact information. A third vehicle then collided into the scene, sending one of the stopped vehicles forward into a 43-year-old man and a 12-year-old child who were standing on the side of the road. Both were rushed to a hospital in critical condition, police originally said. A third person was taken to hospital with minor injuries, and the driver of the third vehicle in the crash was not hurt. Police later confirmed the man and child, both residents of the United States, remain in hospital with serious injuries. m. m.

items.summary: A 12-year-old boy and a 43-year-old man from the United States have been critically injured in a multi-vehicle crash on Highway 403 in Mississauga. m. Paramedics told CTV News Toronto that an adult male and a boy sustained serious, life-threatening injuries and were taken to trauma centres. A third person was taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, paramedics said. S. residents. items.title: Nick Nurse Takes Ontario to Court Over a Denied $700,000 Tax Rebate on His Old Mississauga Home
items.summary: According to INsauga, former Toronto Raptors head coach Nick Nurse has filed a notice of appeal with the Ontario Superior Court after the province denied him and his wife a tax rebate worth nearly $700,000 tied to a Mississauga home they once owned. The dispute centres on the province's Non-Resident Speculation Tax, which stood at 15 per cent for qualifying foreign buyers in the Greater Golden Horseshoe region when the Nurses bought the home in October 2021, a rate the province has since raised to 25 per cent. INsauga reports that under the rules in place at the time, foreign buyers could qualify for a rebate by working continuously in Ontario for at least a year and using the property as a primary residence for at least 60 days. The Nurses sold the home in September 2023, shortly after Nick Nurse's decade-long run with the Raptors ended in April 2023 and he was hired as head coach of the Philadelphia 76ers the following month. The couple applied for the rebate in March 2024, but the Ministry of Finance rejected the claim because they were no longer living in the home when they filed. INsauga reports the Nurses are now arguing in their appeal that the 2021 regulations never actually required them to still be residing in the home at the moment they submitted the application.

items.title: A Financial Drive Restaurant Gets Its First-Ever Red Card From Peel Health Inspectors
items.summary: According to INsauga, Daal Roti Indian Tadka House on Financial Drive in Mississauga was shut down Monday after failing a health inspection. Peel Public Health's report found the restaurant did not properly store food to prevent contamination and did not take adequate measures to prevent pests, among other violations. INsauga reports the restaurant remains closed and can only reopen once it passes a follow-up inspection. This marks the first red card on the restaurant's public inspection record, which INsauga notes goes back to December 2024. A red card is issued when an inspector finds a health risk serious enough that the establishment must close until the danger is removed, distinct from a yellow conditional pass, which flags violations that must be corrected on the spot without forcing a shutdown.

items.title: John Mulaney and Hasan Minhaj Headline a New Outdoor Comedy Festival's Mississauga Debut
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the Great Outdoors Comedy Festival will make its first appearance in the city at Erindale Park from September 11 to 13, bringing stand-up comedy to the Credit River waterfront alongside local food vendors and licensed beverage areas. The city says the lineup includes Emmy-winning comedians John Mulaney, Hasan Minhaj and Ms. Pat, presented by Visit Mississauga as part of its growing slate of major events. The festival, produced by Trixstar Entertainment, launched in 2021 and has since featured performers including Jerry Seinfeld, Kevin Hart, Bill Burr, Amy Schumer and Martin Short at outdoor venues across North America. The City of Mississauga notes this stop will serve as the final date on the festival's 2026 North American tour, and organizers expect it to draw thousands of visitors each day from across the Greater Toronto Area and beyond. Officials say the event is meant to give visitors another reason to spend the weekend in Mississauga while supporting local hotels, restaurants and businesses.

items.title: Heartland Town Centre Adds a Leather Brand, a Global Retailer and a Ramen Spot in 2026
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's Heartland Town Centre at Mavis Road and Britannia Road has picked up a string of new tenants during the first half of 2026. Canadian leather brand Danier, founded in 1972, opened its Heartland location in March, bringing its selection of leather jackets, bags, boots, wallets and accessories to the outdoor shopping centre. INsauga reports Danier has built its reputation over more than 40 years on high-quality leathers and materials. International retailer Miniso opened at Heartland in June, offering beauty products, home decor, electronics, toys, stationery and snacks at affordable prices. INsauga notes Miniso operates more than 5,000 locations worldwide and has run collaborations with brands including Coca-Cola, Marvel, Hello Kitty, Sesame Street and the Beijing Palace Museum. Kinton Ramen has also become one of the shopping centre's most popular stops, serving ramen built on rich broths, signature noodles and a variety of fresh toppings. INsauga says more openings are expected at Heartland before the end of the year.

items.title: Crews Finish the Eastern Tunnels That Will Link Scarborough and Mississauga on One Transit Line
items.summary: According to INsauga, crews have completed excavation of the eastern underground segment of the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, digging twin 500-metre tunnels between Mount Dennis Station and Jane Street. Metrolinx, the provincial agency building the line, says it will operate mainly underground and eventually connect to the already-completed western underground segment, which finished tunnelling back in 2024. At Jane Street, trains will surface onto an elevated guideway running to Scarlett Road before dropping back underground into that western portion of the route. Ontario's transportation minister, Prabmeet Sarkaria, said in a statement that the extension will make it faster and easier for thousands of commuters to get where they're going each day, while also improving connectivity across the GTA and supporting thousands of construction jobs. INsauga reports that once finished, the project will extend Line 5 Eglinton further west, creating nearly 30 kilometres of continuous rapid transit along Eglinton Avenue linking Scarborough, midtown Toronto and Mississauga.

items.title: Peel Highways Brace for 32 Scheduled Closures on Aug. 11
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the province has scheduled 32 separate closures across provincial highways in Peel Region for August 11, 2026. The affected routes include Highway 10, Highway 401, Highway 403, Highway 410, Highway 9 and the Queen Elizabeth Way, the same corridors that carry most commuter and commercial traffic through Mississauga and the surrounding region. Mississauga.com advises drivers to plan their route before heading out given how many highways are affected at once. The outlet's listing does not spell out a reason for this particular round of closures, though its coverage of other recent days has tied similar work to short-term repairs and routine highway maintenance. Anyone driving through Peel this week should build extra time into their trip and watch for detours. Mississauga.com also points readers to a separate closure list for anyone travelling to highways outside Peel Region.
